instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I renew the shop lease, choose: work here with me or take the overseas job. We need to define your promise to 'build this together'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I made that promise before the offer came.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is the point to specify its scope. Are you a working partner or just an investor? Please choose before I enter your name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can send money. That doesn't mean I'm saying goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put 'investor'. Confirm that, please. It means when you promised we'd build it together, you meant the business—not our days in this shop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the spare key or hand it back. Please don't leave it on the edge of the table; we need to settle what last week's 'some space' meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant one quiet evening, not moving out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the key with you. A temporary pause doesn't need a permanent handover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave it here tonight and collect it tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me a collection time, then. 'Tomorrow at six' makes this storage; 'sometime' makes last week the start of leaving. Which should I write beside the key?

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign up for the overnight shift if the project matters to you. Fill the whole slot, please, not just the first hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you put your own name down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm covering decisions, not routine work. Keep the leadership line separate from the shift rota.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. I'll ring you at three if we need a decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only urgent decisions. Put everything else in the morning log. Please don't classify uncertainty as urgency; I need uninterrupted sleep to lead properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give your prize seat to a volunteer if you're serious about the show. I'll organize the handover once I've put my cushion on mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you give yours up too? Our seats are next to each other.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine is an observation position. I need a clear view to assess the staging; please distinguish that from attending.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then swap with me. Same view, and I'll give yours away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move my cushion across first. A seat transfer doesn't include personal equipment. Please don't ask me to assess three hours of staging without proper support.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Win the Smaller Concession
cards.instruction: Get one small surrender, then use its logic to make the larger claim harder to defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: May I put one small pot on the windowsill? I'll measure the base before setting it down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One, as long as it doesn't cover the vent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. These two cuttings can share it. Please judge the footprint, not how many stems are above it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant one plant, not the start of a collection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me which part of the vent the second stem covers. The base hasn't grown. Shall we agree on the space you actually need clear?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Acknowledge that I wrote the opening paragraph of your speech. Please keep that separate from proofreading.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, the opening is yours. I wrote the rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mark where you stop using its argument. A paragraph boundary isn't necessarily a change of reasoning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The conclusion repeats it, but the examples in between are mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the examples. Credit me for the argument in the opening and conclusion, then; please don't call both of those one isolated paragraph.

cards.title: Hide Inside the Callback
cards.instruction: Use an early harmless detail as the explanation for each new consequence, keeping your own role outside the pattern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tent collapsed because of that decorative ribbon. Start your inspection at the ribbon, please, not the fallen poles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tied the ribbon to the support rope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly where a decoration shouldn't be. Please classify the attachment before you start assigning people to it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you pulled the ribbon and the rope came loose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So the ribbon transferred a load. Remove it before we test the rope again; I don't want that decorative fault carried into the rebuild.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That cup started this argument. Move it away from the damaged letter while we work out what happened.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tipped it onto the letter.

beats.speaker: A

beats.text: That's the transfer point, then. Put the cup back in the kitchen; we need a clear desk before tracing where it went wrong.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Answer the Previous Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every dangerous question by sincerely answering an earlier, safer version of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first question was whether it rained. Yes, all evening. Let's take these in order, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm asking why you crashed my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before that, you asked whether the road was wet. It was wet, not flooded; please keep those descriptions separate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you driving too fast for a wet road?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Standing water at the bend, damp surface before it. Please don't reduce both to 'wet'; your road-condition question needs a precise answer before we move on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked where we had lunch and whether it was good. The soup was excellent; I'll answer the two parts separately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was before I asked who ate my birthday cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I hadn't finished the quality part. Excellent soup, slightly too much salt; please don't record an unqualified recommendation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Forget the review. Were you in the kitchen with my cake?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We ate in the cafeteria, not the kitchen. That answers your earlier where question. Please distinguish the dining venue from the place the food was prepared.
